blocking.section: Capacity model (Coefficients K-19, Formulas); Ruralz Control sizing; Re-planning triggers (Control Store volume); Open questions (OQ-capacity-planning-9)
blocking.issue: This is a regression from the L4X-8 fix, and part of the cause is the previous L4X-8 evidence, which wrongly said that Control plane and GitOps defines no Revision retention. Control plane does define one: "Unreferenced Revisions beyond the latest 50 per Environment (target) are deleted." The document now contradicts that dependency in three ways. It tags n_keep as a (hypothesis) with no owner. It says Revision content grows without bound "while no retention exists". It also makes OQ-capacity-planning-9 blocking for Revision retention. The part that really is unbounded, audit segments, is the part the growth row leaves out.
blocking.evidence: K-19: "| K-19 | n_keep, Revisions kept per Environment | 50 (hypothesis) | None | OQ-capacity-planning-9 |"; Formulas: "growth   = f_ro × (s_rev + s_diff + s_src) per day while no retention exists (OQ-capacity-planning-9)"; Ruralz Control sizing: "| Growth without retention, 20 Rollouts per day | 352 MiB per day: 70% of the volume in 19 days (target) [H] |"; OQ-capacity-planning-9: "Which retention and garbage collection apply to Revision content, diffs, sources and audit segments? ... Yes, for Control Store sizing (M2)". Control plane and GitOps, Revision builds: "Unreferenced Revisions beyond the latest 50 per Environment (target) are deleted." Control plane, Audit and security: "the leader seals them into hash-chained segments of at most 4 MiB (target)", with no retention period stated.
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: an operator follows the growth row and prunes Revisions by hand, or resizes for 352 MiB per day that GC already removes. Meanwhile audit segments, the growth nothing bounds, keep growing: 10 MiB per day (hypothesis) with no retention period, plus Revisions still referenced by active, promoted or rollback digests across many Clusters. Fix: tag K-19 as 50 unreferenced Revisions per Environment (target) and cite [Control plane and GitOps](../architecture/04-control-plane-and-gitops.md#building-and-recording-a-revision). Write D_store = E × (50 + referenced Revisions per Environment) × (s_rev + s_diff + s_src) + d_audit × days kept + L_raft + two Raft snapshots. Replace the growth row with audit growth, d_audit per day with no retention, and state when that reaches 70% of the volume. Narrow OQ-capacity-planning-9 to the audit-segment retention period and the count of referenced Revisions. Also point the Control Store volume trigger's "Prune" action at that narrowed question.

blocking.section: Headroom and failure capacity (Zero-Downtime Upgrade on a VM row and the paragraph below the table)
blocking.issue: The row now sizes the host at 2 × container, which fixes the original under-sizing. It still contradicts the handover design it cites, however, and the MAY alternative brings back the OOM. Zero-downtime upgrades and hot reload shares Node-wide ceilings between the old and new process. The new process runs at a soft limit of 90% of the limit minus the old RSS, and only a 0.6 GiB overlap is extra. That is option (b), marked current, of OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-6. That question is owned by capacity-planning and blocks Planned (M1), yet this document never answers it. The row also says each process holds its own `GOMEMLIMIT`, which is option (a). Separately, "halving each C_cap" does not halve M_flood. The unit term min(I_max, C_cap × n_str) × m_u stays at 6,250 MiB once C_cap is 80 or more, so a halved memory split cannot hold a flood.
blocking.evidence: Row: "| Zero-Downtime Upgrade on a VM | Both `ruralzd` processes hold their `GOMEMLIMIT` during Drain (...) | Host memory ≥ 2 × container (hypothesis): 26 GiB for Example 1 (target) |"; paragraph: "Operators MAY instead split 90% of VM memory between both processes' `GOMEMLIMIT` (target), halving each C_cap."; Formulas: "M_flood = ... + min(I_max, C_cap × n_str) × m_u". Zero-downtime upgrades: "Node-wide ceilings are shared: ... the new one admits each ceiling minus that usage, under a soft memory limit of 90% of the limit minus the old RSS (target). Hosts MUST keep the overlap extra free" and "Overlap extra ... about 0.6 GiB plus snapshots (hypothesis)"; OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-6: "(a) Hosts sized for two processes; (b) Shared ceilings, a reduced soft limit and free overlap memory (current) | capacity-planning | Yes, for Planned (M1) in-place handover".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: an Example 1 VM of 13 GiB follows the MAY and gives each process a `GOMEMLIMIT` of about 5.9 GiB. An HTTP/2 header flood during the handover pins 20,000 units at 320 KiB, which is 6,250 MiB, plus M_fix of 1,243 MiB. That is about 7.5 GiB in one process, whatever its C_cap, so the process is OOM-killed in the middle of a Drain and every connection on the Node drops. Fix: answer OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-6 explicitly. Under option (b), the current one, write host memory ≥ container + overlap extra (M_fix − maxBufferedBytes + m_route × R + (K + 2) × s_snap, about 0.6 GiB plus snapshots (hypothesis)): about 13.6 GiB for Example 1 (target). Keep 2 × container only as option (a). Delete the "halving each C_cap" sentence, or replace it with the rule that no split may leave either process below M_flood.

blocking.issue: Acceptance criterion 3 requires every coefficient to cite docs/architecture/12-performance-budgets-and-benchmarking.md. Three rows cite no PB row and name no Open question that would add one. K-22's 0.9 `GOMEMLIMIT` share is in PB's GOGC and GOMEMLIMIT rules, yet the row says "None". K-19 (Revision retention) and K-20 (SM-10 estimate error) are planning parameters owned by Control plane and Vision, not benchmarked coefficients.

PB, GOGC and GOMEMLIMIT rule 1: "operators SHOULD set `GOMEMLIMIT` to about 90% of the container limit (target)". PB Throughput targets: "G1 measures the per-shard GCRA figure behind Scalability's Cell sizing".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: a reader auditing criterion 3 cannot trace K-19, K-20 or K-22 to a verified budget, so the criterion fails and the release-record update rule in Coefficients has nothing to update for them. Fix: cite PB [GOGC and GOMEMLIMIT](../architecture/12-performance-budgets-and-benchmarking.md#gogc-and-gomemlimit) for 0.9, and PB Throughput targets and G1 for the 0.5 shard share, with Scalability as the interim owner. Move K-19 (Control plane, (target)) and K-20 (Vision SM-10, (hypothesis)) out of the coefficient table into Planning inputs, since they are policy and estimate inputs, not benchmark coefficients. Alternatively, keep them and add an Open question to performance-budgets-and-benchmarking that records them in PB.

non_blocking.suggestion: The Memory trigger fires above 70% of `GOMEMLIMIT`. `GOMEMLIMIT` is now sized to the flood floor, 11,981 MiB for Example 1 against M_node of 1,693 MiB, so the trigger stays silent until steady heap is about 5x the plan. By then a coefficient error in K-6 or K-7, which also feeds M_flood, is already invalidating the flood floor. Add a second threshold: heap per connection or per unit more than 10% above K-6 or K-7, or heap above 1.15 × planned M_node (target).

non_blocking.section: Capacity model (Formulas); Headroom and failure capacity
non_blocking.suggestion: N_cpu has no storm term, yet the composite rule requires survivor CPU plus storm to stay at or below 80%. A CPU-bound Cluster that fits exactly (no rounding slack) fails its own check, and no remedy is given. Add λ_storm × (c_hs + c_up) × Z / (Z − 1) to U before computing N_cpu, or lower u_z by the storm share.

Deployment topologies' Sizing defaults still offers option (b): an L4 cap near 2,500 connections in a 4 GiB container. It uses the per-connection formula this document rejects: "an L4 connection cap alone does not bound memory". Say explicitly that option (b) no longer holds and that any Node needs at least M_flood, and link OQ-deployment-topologies-21 beside OQ-capacity-planning-5, so readers of the older table are not misled.

attempts = 1 is justified only by a single `AIModel` candidate. State that the `ai` Upstream has no `retries`, or count retried attempts in the (attempts − 1) × R term, since Scalability's bound counts attempts, not candidates.

non_blocking.section: Headroom and failure capacity; State Store sizing
non_blocking.suggestion: The hot-key check uses λ_key = min(offered, 2 × `requests`). While autoscaling lags the published count, Scalability allows 2 × `requests` × N_serving / N_published calls per window. For an autoscaled Cluster, check λ_key at the lag ratio (up to 2 for Example 1's 6-to-12 range), or require declared ceilings as rule 4 already recommends.
The ADR-0015 link '../adr/0015-zero-downtime-upgrades-so-reuseport.md' still targets a missing file (verify-docs WARN at line 372). Keep it tracked until the ADR lands.
Give the composite zone loss a numeric fail-open bound per key, for example N_serving × ceiling on 4 survivors for about 15 s (hypothesis), not only "15 s of fail-open Rate Limits".
